div.head: Af 1.8
div.ab: Gif þær ðonne oþer mennisc borg sie, bete þone borgbryce swa him ryht wisie, ⁊ ðone wedbryce swa him his scrift scrife.
Gif ðær ðonne oþer mennisc borh sy, bete þone borhbrice swa him riht wisie, ⁊ þone wedbrice swa him his scrift scrife.
Si tunc aliquis plegius intersit, emendet infracturam plegii, sicut rectum edocebit, et infracturam uadii secundum penitentię censuram.
Gif þær ðonne oþer mennisc borg sie, bete þone borgbryce swa him ryht wisie, ⁊ ðone wedbryce swa him his scrift scrife.
Gif þær ðonne oþer mennisc borg sie, bete þone borgbryce swa him ryht wisie, ⁊ ðone wedbryce swa him his scrift scrife.
Wenn aber andere Leute da Bürgen sind, büsse [der Vertragsbrüchige an jene] den Bürgschaftsbruch, wie ihm [weltliches] Recht zuweist, und den Vertragsbruch, wie ihm sein Beichtvater auferlegt.

But if other people are sureties there, let [the one who broke the agreement] compensate [them] for the breach of surety as [secular] law directs him, and for the breach of pledge as his confessor imposes on him.

If, however, other men stand surety for him, he shall pay the compensation [due to them] for violation of bail, as the law directs him, and the compensation for breach of faith, as his confessor prescribes for him.
If, however, there is secular surety for him, he is to pay for the breach of surety as the law directs him, and for the breach of pledge as his confessor prescribes for him.
If other(s) stand(s) surety for him, let him pay for his breach of surety as law indicates, and for the breach of faith as his confessor prescribes.

note.label: compare
note.quote: Compare mennisc borg [...] in §1.8, where the authority invoked is human and not divine.

note.label: compare
note.quote: Significantly, the other instance of self-abandonment in Alfred’s laws, concerning one who has failed to fulfil an oath (cap. 1.8), indicates that part of the compensation is to be determined by a confessor, something which suggests that this and hence the similar clauses were conceived of with penance in mind.

Bessere Übs.: ‘bürgerlich-laienhafte Verbürgung vorliegt’. Der Ggs. ist godborg (s. Gl Bürgschaft 1d) oder að, o. 1—1, 7. Der Versprecher hat hier nicht bloss seinen Glauben in die Hand Geistlicher verpfändet

A better translation: ‘there is a secular, lay suretyship’. The contrast is godborg (see Gl Bürgschaft 1d) or að, above 1—1, 7. Here the promisor has not merely pledged his faith into the hands of clerics
plegius kann auch Bürgenverband heissen. Vgl. Gl Bürgschaftsbruch 1
plegius can also mean a body of sureties. Cf. Gl Bürgschaftsbruch 1

je nach Stand des Bürgen; ebd. Nicht etwa ‘soviel wie Bürge zahlen müsste’ (Marquardsen Haft 25), wenn Versprecher entkäme, das wäre die ursprüngl. Schuld an den Versprechensempfänger (Gläubiger). — Gerichtsversäumnis (s. d. Gl) ist nicht (gegen Price) einziger Fall des Versprechensbruches. Und 1, 8 redet nicht etwa wie 1, 7 vom Entflohenen

according to the rank of the surety; ibid. Not, say, ‘as much as the surety would have to pay’ (Marquardsen Haft 25) if the promisor escaped; that would be the original debt to the recipient of the promise (the creditor). — Default in attending court (see that word in Gl) is not (as against Price) the only case of breach of promise. And 1, 8 does not, say, speak of the fugitive as 1, 7 does
Nicht ‘Beichte’ wie Q versteht, sondern Pfarrer oder wie o. 1, 2⁷, Diözesan
Not ‘confession’, as Q understands it, but the parish priest or, as above 1, 2⁷, the diocesan
